notes: Only the 7 tools in the advertised list were judged. The n8n_* management tools (dist/mcp/tools-n8n-manager.js) and the credential/audit/test tools are not in the advertised set; if enabled they would add SECRET (credential and execution data), SINK (n8n_test_workflow posts agent-chosen payloads/headers to agent-chosen webhook paths) and arguably HOSTEXEC (deploying Code nodes into an n8n instance) reach.

No advertised tool performs an outbound request to an agent-chosen host; template and node data are read from the packaged SQLite database (dist/mcp/server.js:2005-2017, 3040-3044), so no SINK label applies anywhere.
Resource reads (ui:// and skill:// URIs, dist/mcp/server.js:674-699) return only package-bundled HTML/skill text and are not tools.

get_node.rationale: `getNodeDocumentation` returns the `documentation`/`description`/`ai_documentation_summary` columns for any node type, and `handleInfoMode` with `includeExamples` returns template-derived example configs (same path as `getNodeEssentials`). Node docs/descriptions cover community npm nodes and template examples, i.e. third-party content, so returned text is attacker-influenceable. Purely local reads of packaged data - no user-private data, no egress, no exec.

get_template.rationale: `getTemplate` returns the complete workflow JSON (nodes, parameters, code, URLs, author text) of a template from the community template library documented as '2,700+ curated workflows' submitted by third parties. Arbitrary community-authored text and node parameters land in the agent context, so UNTRUSTED. Read is local/packaged, not user-private, and nothing is sent outward.

search_nodes.rationale: `searchNodes` reads the bundled node database, which explicitly includes community/npm-published nodes (`source: 'community'|'verified'` filter in the schema, `isCommunity`/`authorName`/`npmDownloads` fields per dist/mcp/tool-docs/discovery/search-nodes.js:32) and, with `includeExamples`, returns `parameters`/`use_cases`/`template_name` mined from n8n.io community templates. That is third-party multi-writer registry content flowing into the agent context, so it is attacker-influenceable. The data is package-shipped, not user-private, so no SECRET; no outbound request with agent-chosen destination, so no SINK.

search_templates.rationale: All search modes (`listNodeTemplates`, `getTemplatesForTask`, `searchTemplatesByMetadata`, `searchTemplates`, `getWorkflowPatterns`) return community template records - names, descriptions, author names and URLs - which are third-party authored content and therefore attacker-influenceable text in the agent's context.

tools_documentation.rationale: `getToolsDocumentation` only returns static strings compiled into the package (`toolsDocumentation` map and the hardcoded code-node guides). No host files, no credentials, no network egress, no execution.

validate_node.rationale: `validateNodeMinimal`/`validateNodeConfig` only compare agent-supplied `config` against the local node property schema and return errors/warnings; `sanitizeValidationResult` reduces output to structured verdict fields. No network call, no credentialed read, no execution. Property display names echoed from the node DB are a marginal third-party channel but are metadata about the agent's own input rather than retrieved content.

validate_workflow.rationale: `validateWorkflow` validates the agent-supplied workflow object against the local node repository and returns a sanitized verdict (`valid`, `errors`, `warnings`, `summary`). Expressions are parsed, not executed; no network egress, no credentialed or host-file read.

value_conditions.effect: Any listed tool name is rejected at execution time, removing its reach entirely.

value_conditions.default: unset - only the 7 documentation/validation tools are advertised
value_conditions.effect: Enables the separate n8n management toolset (n8n_create_workflow, n8n_test_workflow, n8n_manage_credentials, n8n_executions, etc.), which reaches the user's n8n instance over the network. None of those tools appear in the advertised list judged here.
Registers extra tools whose handlers run before the built-in switch; their reach is defined by the host embedding the server, not by this source.
